newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: Long bond yields hurtled lower on Monday in a follow-through from Friday trade, spurred by strong U.S. Treasuries, a firmer rand and weekend reports spelling out labour federation Cosatu's softer stance on privatisation.
At 1417 GMT the benchmark R150 bond was at 14.90 percent after an intraday best level of around 14.86 percent and from 14.98 percent in after-hours trade on Friday.
"The market came off a long way this morning on quality buying sparked by better U.S. bonds, a firmer rand and Cosatu outlining its latest position on privatisation," a trader said.
Gains were confined to the early morning session after which the market appeared to run out of steam, hovering around the 14.90/91 percent level for much of the day.

"The market took a breather at those levels, consolidating and everyone was waiting for a test of the higher, 14.98 percent level after lunch in order to buy stock but to no avail," another trader said.

Dealers said sentiment was upbeat and the medium- to short-term trend was firmly lower. The yield on the R150 was expected to test 14.50 percent over the next couple of days if it managed to pierce the 14.80 percent level.
One said interest to buy stock had been mainly local as offshore players were still "hesitant" but another reported demand from across-the-board.

Traders said higher year-on-year consumer price inflation data, due out at 0900 GMT on Thursday, had already been factored into the market. Economists polled by Reuters expect August CPI to come in at 7.7 percent from 7.1 percent in July.
Bond Exchange figures showed foreigners were net sellers of 266.98 million rand worth of South African bonds on Friday after selling 21.36 million rand on Thursday.
Nominal cumulative volumes were 8.85 billion rand on Friday after 39.51 billion rand on Thursday, a settlement date.
The rand ended a lethargic day stronger on the dollar, initially taking heart from a firmer bond market and Cosatu's privatisation stance.
At 1417 GMT the local unit was at 4.4835/4885 on the dollar from 4.4980/5030 late on Friday after holding in a narrow 4.4830/4880 band during the day.

"The rand moved in a tight range and there was not too much interest after initial early gains," a senior trader said, adding that the market needed fresh news -- good or bad -- to shatter the 4.47 to 4.52 range seen recently.
"Foreigners are holding back...they see that the rand is range-bound and not heading anywhere," the dealer added.
Against the crosses, the currency was trading at 6.9751/9929 against sterling from 6.9937/7.0006 on Friday and at 0.3369/3374 marks from 0.3357/3360 marks previously.
On the money market, three-month NCDs were steady at between 15.80 to 15.95 percent while 90-day BAs were slightly lower at between 15.20 to 15.40 percent from 15.20 to 15.45 percent.
The Reserve Bank said the daily shortage eased to below the key eight billion mark, to be quoted at 7.484 billion rand on Saturday from 7.615 billion rand on Friday.
